title: Good Enough Never Is
coreMove: Make tolerated drift visible early and attach improvement pressure to the work, not to ego or panic.
sourcePressure: The sidecar supports relentless improvement, demanding institutional standards, anti-complacency pressure, and the distinction between excellence and neurotic perfectionism.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning good enough never is into burnout, perfectionism, or leader impatience instead of a system that refuses invisible decay.

sourceAnchors.name: Good enough never is
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar supports anti-complacency pressure and the difference between excellence and neurotic perfectionism
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The standard is not a mood; it is the visible gap between the work and what the institution promised.

examples: factory defect board with generic red marks

exampleSpecs.domain: blood-test courier network catching small temperature deviations before samples fail
exampleSpecs.audience: Marta, quality lead reviewing route coolers
exampleSpecs.stakes: slight warming can ruin tests while every courier claims the route is basically fine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marta places the temperature strips from three almost-fine routes on the dispatch board and changes cooler loading before a failure appears
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pale blue temperature strips curling beside a cooler latch

exampleSpecs.domain: local newspaper copy desk catching headline corrections that readers never complain about
exampleSpecs.audience: Matthew, managing editor after a clean-looking week
exampleSpecs.stakes: small corrections can teach the newsroom to accept fuzziness in public facts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew stacks silent corrections by type, then makes the desk fix the upstream checklist instead of celebrating no complaints
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a neat pile of correction slips under the newsroom clock

exampleSpecs.domain: craft brewery refusing small packaging scuffs before distributors normalize them
exampleSpecs.audience: Giulia, packaging manager under a holiday shipment deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: brand trust erodes when small scuffs become the accepted look
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 11:18 p.m., Giulia stops the labeler for a three-millimeter drift and logs the fix as standard protection, not personal fussiness
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a label edge sitting three millimeters low under inspection light
mustAvoid: aesthetic nitpicking with no customer promise

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal snow-removal team reviewing blocks that were technically cleared but unsafe for wheelchairs
exampleSpecs.audience: Devon, accessibility coordinator after a mild storm
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents can be trapped by snow lips everyone calls acceptable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What counts as cleared if a wheelchair cannot cross? Devon uses curb photos to update the route signoff standard
exampleSpecs.firstImage: curb-cut photos with snow ridges casting thin shadows
mustAvoid: weather complaint as generic civic gripe

exampleSpecs.domain: meal-kit company tracking recipe substitutions that technically work but weaken trust
exampleSpecs.audience: Chloe, culinary operations lead reading customer notes
exampleSpecs.stakes: small swaps can make the promise of reliable cooking feel arbitrary
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Would you cook from us again after the third substitution?" Chloe asks, then changes procurement triggers before churn shows up
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three recipe cards with different substituted ingredients circled
mustAvoid: food preference as the whole problem

exampleSpecs.domain: airport cleaning contractor refusing invisible restroom drift during overnight audits
exampleSpecs.audience: Henrik, contract manager whose metrics all show green
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contract can be lost when passengers sense decline before metrics catch it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Henrik run a white-glove audit under stall hinges and change supervisor walks even though the dashboard is green
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a white cotton glove gray at the fingertip under fluorescent restroom light

skillTargets: spot tolerated drift before visible failure
choose pressure mechanisms tied to the work

tryThisNowSpec: Find one place where the phrase basically fine appears. Replace it with the visible standard, the smallest unacceptable drift, and who checks it next.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
